text:
maria: FYI seeing persistent KV cache growth on longctx tests with mixed H100/MI250x runs. start of thread with initial traces.

sam: logs? small repro?

maria: minimal repro attached below. runs for ~10k tokens then memory climbs ~200MB per minute until OOM on MI node.

chao: any recent changes to kernel selection or batching?

maria: yep - last week we flipped kernel selector to prefer tiled-accel for short prefixes (to optimize latency) and bumped aggressive prefetch in batching heuristics. both landed in runtime v2.3.1.

yumi: could be prefetcher pulling in pages that then get evicted out-of-order across GPUs. That can fragment the page table and reduce reuse.

maria: here's the critical log chunk from the MI250x job:

```
[2026-02-14 14:02:12] kvcache: page_alloc id=0x7fffc, size=2MB, seq=32768
[2026-02-14 14:02:12] pt_walk: miss wp=0x3a4, latency=19ms, tlb_miss=1
[2026-02-14 14:02:13] kvcache: evict id=0x3b2 owner=H100 shard=1 reason=soft_watermark
[2026-02-14 14:02:15] pt_remap: remap_count=8, fragmented=1
[2026-02-14 14:02:15] memory: resident=13.6GB -> 14.1GB (growth +500MB)
```

sam: interesting, remap_count spikes line up with prefetch windows. on H100 nodes we see nvlink stalls at the same timestamps.

chao: hypothesis: tiled kernel selection reduces per-op compute time so batching pushes more outstanding KV prefetches, which increases concurrent page allocations and causes the PT to fragment. when eviction policy runs, it evicts pages that were soon-to-be-reused, causing reuse ratio collapse and growth as we keep reloading the same pages.

maria: repro steps I used: `./perf_run --model paged-attn --seq 32768 --batch 6 --prefetch=2 --kernels=auto` on mixed cluster (2xH100 + 1xMI250x). after ~6k tokens memory slope increases.

yumi: can you paste the KV reuse stats? we added counters last quarter but need the slice.

maria: paste: `kv.reuse.ratio=0.19`, `kv.pt.frag=0.32`, `kv.evictions.soft=412`, `kv.evictions.hard=3` (over 20m).

sam: reuse ratio under 0.2 is bad. prior baseline with kernels locked to generic produced ~0.48 reuse and stable memory.

chao: quick mitigation ideas: dampen prefetch window when mixed-arch cluster detected; add a streaming backpressure so the kernel selector doesn't aggressively prioritize tiny-latency kernels for large-seq workloads; introduce an eviction bias that prefers pages with low future-use score rather than LRU-only.

maria: I prototyped two quick fixes: 1) prefetchoff on MI250x nodes, 2) soft-evict watermark lowered from 0.85 to 0.7. both reduced growth but only the prefetch change avoided the remap spikes.

sam: any signs of metadata corruption (ghost pointers)? logs you pasted show remap_count > 1 but no corrupt ptrs.

maria: correct, no panic/corrupt pointers so far, just high fragmentation and repeated remaps.

yumi: do we see different behavior when sequence distribution skews (many short vs one long)?

maria: yes — many short-seq workloads still fine. the problem surfaces when a single long context dominates and when kernel selector flips to tiled. batching and prefetch interplay seems crucial.

chao: action plan:
- add telemetry: `kv.pt.evictions_reason`, `kv.prefetch.outstanding`, `kv.kernel.choice`
- gate tiled kernel pick behind reuse_ratio >= 0.35 for seq > 16k
- add eviction policy experiment: prefer eviction of pages with low future_use_prob (from LRU+predictor)
- run mixed-arch canary with prefetch disabled on MI250x

sam: agree. also let's add a short flamegraph capture around pt_walk and page_alloc to compare H100 vs MI. use nvprof + rocprof for parity.

maria: I can run the canary tomorrow and post traces. initial diff showed pt_walk latency 12-22ms on MI vs 4-8ms on H100 for the same ops.

devops-bot: staging-canary deploy `kv-prefetch-gate` succeeded on cluster-mixed at 2026-02-15T02:10:00Z

maria: canary results: with prefetch disabled on MI nodes the reuse_ratio jumped to 0.46 and memory stabilized. with prefetch enabled but gated kernel selection we saw partial improvement (reuse ~0.31).

chao: that implies two orthogonal causes: 1) prefetch aggressiveness causing cross-GPU fragmentation, 2) kernel choice altering request concurrency and therefore prefetch footprint.

sam: next steps for PRs:
- runtime: add `reuse_ratio` guard in kernel_selector (PR #4521)
- runtime: add `kv.prefetch.max_outstanding` knob with default conservative value on MI/AMD
- telemetry: add the counters yumi listed to telemetry schema
- infra: add mixed-arch perf job to daily CI for longctx workloads

maria: assigning: sam -> kernel_selector PR, chao -> eviction predictor spike, yumi -> telemetry schema, maria -> canary runs & traces.

yumi: also document the debugging artifacts in eng-runtime/diagnostics so we remember exact flags and commands.

maria: filed follow-ups and linked traces in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-2345. closing for now, will re-open if canary regressions. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks team — solid investigation. keep an eye on perf jobs overnight.

chao: one more note: consider adding a small PT compaction pass when fragmentation metric exceeds threshold to reduce remap churn longterm.

maria: noted. will prototype compaction in a branch after the immediate patches.
